messages:
Liam (Customer): Hey team — hitting 429s intermittently during a load test. We were on free tier, just switched some traffic to paid but still seeing bursts failing. Only started after we rotated keys yesterday. Any quick checklists?
Maya (Support): sorry to hear that, Liam. Can you paste the exact error payload you see? 429 usually rate limit but could be auth.
Liam (Customer): here's the header-ish output we get in our app log: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, body: `\{"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\", \"retry_after\": 30}`. We also get lots of `401 Unauthorized` for a few attempts right after we rotated the API key.
Maya (Support): thanks. Two parallel issues possible: (1) token/key not propagated to all services causing 401s and retry storms, (2) subsequent retries causing quota exhaustion and 429s. Can you confirm you updated all hosts and any CI/CD runners?
Liam (Customer): we updated the app servers but forgot the ingestion lambda. Doh. That lambda kept replaying old requests for ~10 minutes.
Maya (Support): that explains the retry storm. For immediate mitigation: stop the lambda or throttle it, rotate the old key to revoke, and we can request a temporary burst increase while you clean up.
Liam (Customer): stopping lambda now... done. 401s dropping, but still seeing 429s from some clients.
Maya (Support): okay I'll pull rate-limit telemetry. tagging eng-sre: @Jon can you eyeball account 55421's rate buckets? I see repeated `retry_after` values in the logs.
Jon (Eng-SRE): looking. I can see a burst at 2026-03-11T14:02Z where 12k requests hit within 60s. Most of them came from the IP range associated with the lambda. The account is currently on Free tier caps: 60 req/min. They've transitioned some routes to paid but the old key kept hitting free-tier buckets because the old key belonged to the legacy project.
Maya (Support): thanks, Jon. Can we confirm whether those legacy keys can be disabled server-side to stop excess traffic?
Jon (Eng-SRE): I disabled the legacy API key for account 55421 at 14:12Z. That should immediately stop any traffic using it. Also temporarily lifted burst quota by +3x for 10 minutes to let them finish outstanding requests — logged as temporary exception TICKET-8873.
rate-limiter-bot: Automatic note: temporary burst exception applied to account 55421 until 2026-03-11T14:22Z. Reason: customer-side replayed traffic after key rotation.
Liam (Customer): thank you — we see errors tailing off. A couple follow-ups: (1) how do we avoid this in future? (2) if we upgrade to paid, what's the process for permanent higher caps / sales assist?
Maya (Support): good questions. For (1) standard pattern: have a key rotation playbook that updates all consumers, add a short grace period where both keys are valid, and implement client-side backoff (exponential jitter) to avoid synchronized retries. We can share our docs snippet.
Maya (Support): for (2), Priya from Sales can explain upgrade paths. Priya, can you advise on paid tier options and how quickly we can provision higher sustained QPS for this account?
Priya (Sales): hi all — we can do two things: (A) self-serve upgrade to Paid Starter for predictable higher caps (~5k req/min) which is instant, (B) sales-assisted Dedicated quota or a Reserved Capacity plan for guaranteed throughput and SLA. For rush cases we can provision an interim uplift once we validate account and payment method.
Liam (Customer): our traffic pattern is spiky — a burst-oriented quota with short surge windows would be ideal. Is there a documented handoff path so we don't lose time during sales ops?
Priya (Sales): yes. I’ll create a short checklist: verify billing, fill the surge request form, agree to temporary uplift terms (duration, caps), then we coordinate with Eng-SRE to apply. Typical turnaround for the temporary uplift is ~2 hours during business hours. Permanent Dedicated requires contract but we can fast-track when needed.
Maya (Support): I'll attach a template in a minute. Meanwhile, Jon — any artifact we should capture for postmortem?
Jon (Eng-SRE): capture the replayed request IDs, rate bucket deltas, and the lambda's invocation logs. I recommend adding a monitoring rule: alert if a single key issues >500 req/min for >1m. That would have caught this earlier.
Liam (Customer): noted. We can add the alert on our side too. Also, can you share the exact steps you took to disable the legacy key? I want to include that in our runbook.
Maya (Support): steps: 1) identify key id from our admin console (filter by creation date and owner), 2) revoke key (this revokes tokens immediately), 3) confirm no traffic for 2m in rate telemetry, 4) if needed, apply temporary burst uplift. We did that in the admin UI and logged ticket TICKET-8873.
Maya (Support): here's the quick config snippet for client backoff we recommend: ```js
// exponential backoff with jitter
async function callWithRetry(fn, attempts=5) {
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try{return await fn()}catch(e){
      const base = Math.pow(2,i)*100; // ms
      const jitter = Math.random()*100;
      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, base + jitter));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('retries exhausted');
}
```
Liam (Customer): great, we'll put that in. One more: billing — we saw a small unexpected charge when the account briefly hit the paid flows. Will that be prorated or reversed if we end up staying on free?
Priya (Sales): charges are prorated for the billing period. If you stay on free and the usage bump was an accidental surge, we can open a goodwill review. Please DM me the account id and invoice number and I'll follow up.
rate-limiter-bot: Note: per-policy, account-level temporary exceptions are logged and visible to security/audit.
Maya (Support): action items: (1) Liam: validate all tokens rotated and remove legacy keys, (2) Liam: add client-side backoff and alerting, (3) Priya: initiate surge uplift process if needed, (4) Jon: document metrics and mark for postmortem.
Liam (Customer): thanks everyone. Really appreciate the fast help. I'll follow up after the runbook changes.
Priya (Sales): ping me once you want the uplift; I can start verification.
Jon (Eng-SRE): i'll dump the relevant rate histograms to the ticket.
Maya (Support): closing here for now — re-open if 429s persist. :thumbsup:
